markdown_content: # Pattern Drafter | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive This document details the new Pattern Drafter feature in Clo 2025.0, explaining its interface, functionality, measurement management, pattern creation workflow, AI integration, and design tools. It is optimized for understanding parametric pattern drafting, measurement handling, and AI-assisted design generation in Clo. --- ## Introduction to Pattern Drafter in Clo 2025.0 This section introduces the Pattern Drafter, an improved parametric pattern tool in Clo 2025.0 designed to facilitate faster and easier garment design by automating pattern creation and arrangement. - Pattern Drafter replaces the previous parametric pattern tool. - It allows users to quickly draft initial patterns that are automatically sewn and arranged on avatars in the 3D window. - The feature streamlines the early stages of design, enabling rapid iteration and idea visualization. --- ## Accessing Pattern Drafter and Basic Workflow This section explains how to access the Pattern Drafter in Clo, load avatars for fitting context, and the initial pattern creation steps. - Open Clo and bring in a 3D avatar from the library (e.g., female avatar) for accurate pattern fitting and automatic sewing. - Pattern Drafter is found in the top toolbar under the 2D tools menu. - Upon activation, the interface shows options for garment type, fit categories, and measurement sets. - Currently, only shirt types are supported with different fit styles such as set-in sleeves, raglan, and drop shoulder. - The tool automatically arranges drafted patterns on the avatar in the 3D window for immediate preview. --- ## Measurement Management and Customization This section covers how measurements are displayed, selected, and customized within the Pattern Drafter interface. - Measurements are grouped by garment parts: front body, back body, sleeves, cuffs, front hem, back hem. - Eye icons allow users to show/hide sections. - Measurement types include: - **General:** Default, comprehensive set of core points of measurement (POMs), suited for quotes and spec pages. - **Simplified:** Reduced number of measurements for quick input. - **Custom (Set Detail):** Allows users to select/deselect individual measurements for full control. - Symmetry options: - **Symmetry:** Creates half symmetrical patterns. - **Half Symmetry:** Unfolds symmetrical halves of a single pattern. - Measurements can be reset individually or all at once. - Some measurements have dropdown options for selecting measurement origin points (e.g., high point shoulder, center front). --- ## Loading and Using CSV Specs for Pattern Drafting This section explains integration with CSV files for managing pattern specifications. - Users can open CSV spec files containing measurements pre-formatted for Pattern Drafter. - Saving a current spec setup as a CSV template is possible for repeated use. - Templates facilitate easy editing and rapid loading of measurement data. - Once a spec is loaded, pressing the **Create** button generates the pattern draft automatically. --- ## Pattern Drafting Workflow Examples: Drop Shoulder and Raglan Fits This section demonstrates pattern drafting using different fit types and how measurements differ between them. - Selecting a fit type (e.g., drop shoulder) updates the measurement requirements accordingly. - Measurements for drop shoulder include front/back bust, armhole length, hem, sleeve length, etc. - Raglan fit has distinct measurements such as raglan front/back, raglan neck front/back. - Users can toggle and customize these measurement sets via the **Set Detail** option. - The interface provides visual dotted lines indicating which parts of the pattern will be affected by measurement changes. - Measurements can be adjusted interactively by dragging, arrow keys, or typing values. - The "Total" option on some measurements links front and back pattern dimensions, locking one when the other is edited to maintain consistency. --- ## Important Notes on Pattern Drafter Purpose and Limitations This section clarifies the intended use and limitations of the Pattern Drafter tool. - Pattern Drafter is a conceptual drafting tool, **not for final production-ready patterns**. - It provides the first draft or idea of a pattern quickly and easily. - Final adjustments and refinements require manual editing using Clo’s design tools. - Users’ domain knowledge and vision are essential to finalize patterns. - The tool relies on established garment science but is designed for rapid prototyping rather than precision engineering. --- ## Pattern Editing and Design Tools Post-Drafting This section details the design tools available in Clo for refining patterns after initial drafting. - After creating a draft, users can manually move, resize, and reorder pattern pieces in the 2D window for better arrangement. - Tools include: - **Optimize Curve Points:** Simplifies curve points for easier editing. - **Change Length:** Adjusts pattern segment lengths uniformly. - **Match Up / Match Measurement:** Aligns edges and matches measurements between pattern pieces. - **Scale and Move:** Quickly resizes and repositions segments or whole patterns. - Style line tools and 3D garment pen tools are available for detailed shape editing. - These tools enable fast, iterative refinement of the initial draft to better match design intent. --- ## AI-Assisted Pattern Generation Using the Magic Wand This section explains the AI-powered feature integrated into Pattern Drafter to generate pattern designs from prompts or sketches. - Located next to the fit selection is a magic wand icon providing AI pattern generation. - Two modes are supported: - **Prompt-based Generation:** Users can write descriptive prompts (e.g., "cropped loose fit, v-neck, short sleeve") to generate pattern images. - **Image Upload:** Users can upload flat sketch images of garments to generate patterns. - Generated images appear with garment sketches, and users can pick from multiple variations via the history tab. - After generation, patterns are automatically populated in Pattern Drafter’s measurement fields. - Users can then create and simulate these patterns on the avatar immediately. --- ## Best Practices for AI Image-Based Pattern Generation This section advises on optimizing image uploads for better AI generation accuracy. - Use high-quality flat sketches with clear outlines. - Sketches should have distinctly visible seam lines and minimal ambiguity. - Avoid folded or unclear sketches for best results. - Clean, flat, schematic sketches yield the most accurate generated patterns. --- ## Post-Generation Editing and Refinement of AI-Generated Patterns This section highlights the ability to adjust AI-generated patterns using measurement fields and editing tools. - Once generated, users can manually adjust measurements like neck width, neck drop, sleeve length, hem length, etc. - Pattern pieces can be moved or resized using the 2D pattern tools. - Curve optimization and style lines help refine shapes. - This flexibility allows rapid iteration between AI-assisted design generation and manual customization. --- # Summary The Clo 2025.0 Pattern Drafter is a powerful parametric tool designed for rapid garment pattern prototyping. It supports detailed measurement management, CSV spec integration, and multiple fit types. Users can draft basic patterns quickly, then refine them with Clo’s comprehensive design tools. The integration of AI-assisted generation from text prompts or sketches enhances creativity and speeds up the early design phase. Pattern Drafter serves as a first draft tool to accelerate visualization and iteration, with final pattern production requiring user expertise and manual refinement.

chunks.content: - Saving a current spec setup as a CSV template is possible for repeated use. - Templates facilitate easy editing and rapid loading of measurement data. - Once a spec is loaded, pressing the **Create** button generates the pattern draft automatically. --- ## Pattern Drafting Workflow Examples: Drop Shoulder and Raglan Fits This section demonstrates pattern drafting using different fit types and how measurements differ between them. - Selecting a fit type (e.g., drop shoulder) updates the measurement requirements accordingly. - Measurements for drop shoulder include front/back bust, armhole length, hem, sleeve length, etc. - Raglan fit has distinct measurements such as raglan front/back, raglan neck front/back. - Users can toggle and customize these measurement sets via the **Set Detail** option. - The interface provides visual dotted lines indicating which parts of the pattern will be affected by measurement changes. - Measurements can be adjusted interactively by dragging, arrow keys, or typing values. - The "Total" option on some measurements links front and back pattern dimensions, locking one when the other is edited to maintain consistency. --- ## Important Notes on Pattern Drafter Purpose and Limitations This section clarifies the intended use and limitations of the Pattern Drafter tool. - Pattern Drafter is a conceptual drafting tool, **not for final production-ready patterns**. - It provides the first draft or idea of a pattern quickly and easily. - Final adjustments and refinements require manual editing using Clo’s design tools. - Users’ domain knowledge and vision are essential to finalize patterns. - The tool relies on established garment science but is designed for rapid prototyping rather than precision engineering. --- ## Pattern Editing and Design Tools Post-Drafting This section details the design tools available in Clo for refining patterns after initial drafting. - After creating a draft, users can manually move, resize, and reorder pattern pieces in the 2D window for better arrangement. - Tools include: - **Optimize Curve Points:** Simplifies curve points for easier editing. - **Change Length:** Adjusts pattern segment lengths uniformly. - **Match Up / Match Measurement:** Aligns edges and matches measurements between pattern pieces. - **Scale and Move:** Quickly resizes and repositions segments or whole patterns. - Style line tools and 3D garment pen tools are available for detailed shape editing. - These tools enable fast, iterative refinement of the initial draft to better match design intent. --- ## AI-Assisted Pattern Generation Using the Magic Wand This section explains the AI-powered feature integrated into Pattern Drafter to generate pattern designs from prompts or sketches. - Located next to the fit selection is a magic wand icon providing AI pattern generation. - Two modes are supported: - **Prompt-based Generation:** Users can write descriptive prompts (e.g., "cropped loose fit, v-neck, short sleeve") to generate pattern images. - **Image Upload:** Users can upload flat sketch images of garments to generate patterns. - Generated images appear with garment sketches, and users can pick from multiple variations via the history tab. - After generation, patterns are automatically populated in Pattern Drafter’s measurement fields.

It supports detailed measurement management, CSV spec integration, and multiple fit types. Users can draft basic patterns quickly, then refine them with Clo’s comprehensive design tools. The integration of AI-assisted generation from text prompts or sketches enhances creativity and speeds up the early design phase. Pattern Drafter serves as a first draft tool to accelerate visualization and iteration, with final pattern production requiring user expertise and manual refinement.
